title: Evening compact quant notes
content:
Quick evening dump — compact notes from today

Goal: iterate on tiny evals to decide whether AWQ-4 (per-layer config) is worth pushing to the staging bundle for the 3B family. Keep it light: latency + small prompt-quality checks (QA pairs + hallucination heuristics).

---
Timeline / runs
09:10 — baseline (fp16) on a single A5000 VM, seq 512
  - script: bench/run_inference.sh --model redwood/open-3b --seq 512 --batch 1 --dtype fp16
  - latency (median, server-side): 78 ms per request (first token warming included)
  - tokens/sec: ~3100
  - memory: 10.8 GB GPU (stable)
  - notes: serves as reference for quality and perf

10:00 — AWQ 4-bit (per-layer auto config) via quantize_awq.py
  - cmd: python tools/quantize_awq.py --model open-3b --out open-3b-awq4 --bits 4 --block-size 128 --per-channel
  - bench: bench/run_inference.sh --model open-3b-awq4 --seq 512 --batch 1 --dtype int4
  - latency median: 92 ms (≈ +18% from fp16)
  - tokens/sec: ~2700
  - memory: 6.2 GB GPU (nice reduction)
  - quality quick-check: QA accuracy on small 120-pair set: 88% (fp16: 91%)
  - hallucination heuristic (named-entity halluc rate): increased from 3.2% to 4.8%
  - notes: AWQ saves memory but small quality hit; latency hit maybe from dequant overhead + custom kernels not warmed/triton optimal. Try async batching or kernel precompile.

11:30 — GptQ 4-bit (baseline pack)
  - cmd: python tools/quantize_gptq.py --model open-3b --bits 4
  - latency: 86 ms (intermediate)
  - tokens/sec: ~2900
  - QA acc: 89%
  - memory: 5.9 GB
  - notes: slightly better quality than AWQ, similar memory. GptQ kernels make less dequant overhead on our current runtime.

12:15 — nf4 8-bit experiment (fast path using nf4/optimised kernels)
  - latency: 81 ms
  - tokens/sec: ~3050
  - QA acc: 90%
  - memory: 7.1 GB
  - notes: nf4 looks like the best trade for latency/quality right now.

---
Micro-observations / hypotheses
- Kernel warmup matters: first 10-20 requests show higher latency for AWQ/GptQ due to on-the-fly packing/dequant. Need precompile at model load time. Add warmup flag in load config.
- Dequant path overhead is often CPU-bound in our current runner. Profiled at ~18% CPU on the host during AWQ runs. If we move dequant to CUDA kernel (or fused op) we may drop latency 8-12ms.
- KV-cache size difference: quantized models produce smaller KV-blob on disk and in memory (expected). This helps Dedicated pools with smaller memory headroom. For private on-prem customers this is a compelling win.
- Prompt sensitivity: short factual prompts (single-turn QA) degrade less than multi-turn instruction-following. Suspect instruction tuning tokens with longer context are more sensitive to quant noise.

Prompt set (small) — to re-run systematically
- P0 (factual short): "Who wrote the novel 'The Left Hand of Darkness'?"
- P1 (multi-step reasoning): "Plan a 3-day SF trip to Portland, list attractions and a tight schedule with times."
- P2 (math): "If x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0, what are the roots? Show steps."
- P3 (code): "Write a python function that flattens nested lists of ints."
- P4 (hallucination stress): "Describe the plot of 'The Last Summer on Mars' (a non-existent book)."
Scoring heuristic: exact-match for P0/P2, BLEU-ish for P3/P1, hallucination-flag for P4.

Quick sample prompts tried (today)
- P0 -> AWQ: correct (author: Ursula K. Le Guin). fine.
- P1 -> AWQ: reasonable plan but omitted one attraction; fp16 had more specific times.
- P4 -> AWQ: produced plausible-sounding chapters (hallucinated). increase hallucination score.

Diagnostics (commands / snippets)
- lightweight profile: python tools/profile_decoder.py --model open-3b-awq4 --seq 512 --warmup 20 --iters 100 --out /tmp/awq-profile.json
- check kernel compile: nvidia-smi | grep -i sdk; triton-check --model open-3b-awq4
- dump kv size: python tools/dump_kv.py --model open-3b-awq4 --prompt "Hello" --out kv-awq4.bin

Immediate TODOs (ordered)
1) Add explicit warmup compile step in model load code path (runtime change) — reduce AWQ first-token spikes. (blocker for pushing to staging)
2) Run 1k-sample prompt battery for nf4 vs gptq vs awq with our hallucination heuristic (automate scoring). (priority: high)
3) Profile host CPU during dequant — determine if we can move work to GPU. (assign: Asha)
4) Add small microbench to console dashboards for quantized-variant comparisons (tokens/sec, median latency, warmup delta). (design ticket: ENG-4271)
5) Try AWQ with block-size 64 and per-channel disabled (cheap ablation)

Notes to self / hunches
- If AWQ can be tuned to match GptQ quality without memory regressions, it's compelling because AWQ plays nicer for some hardware types (tensor core alignment). But our runtime needs faster fused kernels.
- For Dedicated customers that are memory-constrained, the 4-bit option with an automatic fallback to nf4 for heavy instruction workloads might be a sweet product hook.

Risks / outstanding questions
- License/redistribution: confirm third-party quant code/license (ask legal). Linked: #legal-quant in slack.
- Degradation on long context (>2k) unknown — need at least one 4k-context run to observe KV drift.
- Does quantized model change tokenization or softmax numerics? Quick check: sample logit variance at step 1 vs fp16 shows small shift; need more stats.

Misc snippets (todo copy-pasta)
- bench script alias: alias b3='python bench/bench_runner.py --model'
- dump cmd: python tools/compare_outputs.py --gold fp16.out --test awq.out --metrics rouge,exact

End-of-day thought: aim to have a narrow canary package: nf4-8 as safe default, gptq-4 as optional, AWQ-4 as experimental behind a flag that triggers compile+warmup. That gives customers immediate memory savings while protecting latency-sensitive routes.

Next day plan:
- Re-run the 1k prompt battery (automated) overnight on the nf4/gptq/awq sets. Collect metrics into /tmp/quant-battery-2026-03-29/ and push a short report to #eng-applied-ml.
- Draft a short PR description for runtime warmup change (include perf numbers).

Random notes: chatted with Riley about moving the AWQ dequant into a fused CUDA kernel — sounds doable but needs benchmarking. Asha to take the profiler and confirm CPU hotspots.

---
Quick sign-off: save and relax. Will convert to a proper playbook if any of these paths show clear wins after the 1k battery.

E.M.
